title: Interactions Between Running Volume and Running Pace and Injury Occurrence in Recreational Runners: A Secondary Analysis
authors: Ramskov D, Rasmussen S, Sorensen H, Parner ET, Lind M, Nielsen R
population: Injury-free Danish recreational runners, 24-week follow-up with GPS data, secondary analysis of a randomised-trial dataset
findings: 586 injury-free recreational runners analysed; 133 sustained an RRI over 24 weeks of GPS follow-up.

Interaction of a relative weekly volume progression above 10% with pace progression: risk difference 8.1% (95% CI -9.3% to 25.6%), not a statistically significant positive interaction on the additive scale.
Interaction of an absolute weekly volume progression above 5 km with pace progression: risk difference 5.2% (95% CI -12.0% to 22.5%), also not significant.
The study tests the interaction between volume and pace progression, not the main effect of the 10% rule.
limitations: Abstract-level verification only. Wide confidence intervals mean the study cannot exclude a positive interaction; secondary analysis of a trial dataset; additive-scale interaction only. A null interaction is not evidence that a 10% weekly rule is safe or unsafe.
implications: No evidence here to add a combined pace-and-volume progression rule. Keep intensity progression handled separately from the distance ramp.
Absolute (5 km) and relative (10%) weekly-increase definitions gave similarly imprecise interaction estimates; either can be used as a convention without evidence preferring one.
